children: A higher offer from German chemicals group BASF
will not be enough to secure a takeover of smaller peer Evonik
, two people close to Evonik told Reuters on Wednesday, saying a deal would also need a compelling industrial rationale.
BASF first approached its smaller ​rival in September, but Evonik has resisted the advances and recently rejected ⁠a sweetened offer of over €11 billion ($12 billion).
In an internal memo seen by Reuters, Evonik's management told employees it remained convinced the company had a strong future as a standalone business.

The comments come after German business publication Handelsblatt, citing financial industry sources, reported that BASF would need to significantly raise its offer for Evonik, with a bid of €26 to €28 per share potentially helping to break the deadlock.
Evonik and BASF both declined to comment on the report.
On Tuesday, sources told Reuters that the chemicals giant was preparing to offer greater concessions to Evonik in its latest attempt to secure support for the deal.

BASF has approached the state ​government in North Rhine-Westphalia, where Evonik is based, and its top shareholder, ​the RAG Foundation, with a letter offering possible commitments to plants, jobs and training, the sources said.
